H&P – Super Detailed  

Consult Summary:  
45-year-old non-smoking woman with systemic lupus erythematosus on methotrexate presented via video consult with same-day onset of pleuritic right-sided back pain, mild dyspnoea, subjective fever, and two episodes of scant haemoptysis; appears hemodynamically stable on limited virtual exam but requires in-person chest examination to rule out community-acquired pneumonia versus pulmonary embolism or other causes.

History:
• Presenting complaint – “Feeling very breathless” with sharp pain in right posterior chest/back on deep inspiration.  
• Onset/progression – Began earlier today; pain and dyspnoea sudden in onset.  
• Associated symptoms – Subjective “slight fever” (not formally measured), two episodes of coughing up blood-tinged sputum, awareness of heartbeat; denies recent long-haul flight, leg pain, or swelling.  
• Two-week history – Fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, daily activities more difficult.  
• No report of chills, weight loss, night sweats, sputum production (other than blood), calf pain, or recent trauma.  
• Review of systems otherwise not explored/recorded.

Past Medical History:
• Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) – on methotrexate; no other flare features reported today.  
• No history of DVT/PE or other chronic illnesses mentioned.

Medications:  
• Methotrexate – dose/route/frequency not documented; last dose taken this morning.

Allergies:  
• No known drug or other allergies.

Social History:
• Lives alone in a flat; owns a cat.  
• Occupation: Office desk job.  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol/recreational drugs: Not discussed.  
• Recent travel: No recent long-haul flights.

Family History:
• No known family history of venous thrombo-embolism or bleeding/clotting disorders; other family history not discussed.

Physical Examination: (virtual)
• General: Appears clinically stable, converses in full sentences.  
• Vitals: Radial pulse counted at 66–74 bpm, regular. Temperature, BP, RR, SpO₂ not measured.  
• Skin/perfusion: Capillary refill brisk.  
• HEENT: Oropharynx normal on video; no cervical lymphadenopathy.  
• Neck: Self-palpation negative for enlarged nodes.  
• Cardiovascular/Respiratory/Abdomen/Neuro: Not examined on video.

Investigations:
• None performed to date.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Acute pleuritic pain, dyspnoea, haemoptysis  
  Assessment: Likely community-acquired pneumonia or other chest infection; differentials include pulmonary embolism (PE) given SLE, and methotrexate-related lung toxicity.  
  Plan:  
  • Same-day face-to-face GP review arranged for full vitals, chest auscultation, and blood pressure.  
  • Consider chest X-ray and baseline bloods if examination suggests infection or other pathology.  
  • Empiric oral antibiotic to be considered after in-person assessment if pneumonia confirmed (no antibiotic prescribed yet).  
  • If PE suspected clinically, arrange D-dimer and/or urgent imaging per local protocol.  
  • Advise patient to seek emergency care if worsening breathlessness, chest pain, syncope, or increased haemoptysis.

Issue 2 – Immunosuppression (Methotrexate + SLE)  
  Assessment: Heightened infection risk; possible drug-induced pneumonitis.  
  Plan:  
  • Review need to temporarily withhold methotrexate pending diagnostic clarification (to be decided after in-person assessment or rheumatology advice).  
  • Ensure follow-up with rheumatology or primary care for SLE monitoring.

Issue 3 – Patient anxiety re: lung cancer  
  Assessment: Low immediate likelihood, but concern acknowledged.  
  Plan:  
  • Reassured that presentation more suggestive of infection.  
  • Will consider follow-up chest X-ray if symptoms persist or fail to improve.

General plan items:  
• Provide clinic support line number for scheduling same-day appointment.  
• Document allergy status and medication list at next visit.  
• Safety-net: return for any deterioration.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Community-acquired pneumonia – High likelihood: sudden fever, pleuritic pain, cough with haemoptysis; immunosuppressed host.  
2. Pulmonary embolism – Moderate likelihood: classic triad present and SLE predisposes to thrombosis, though pulse normal and no travel/surgery risk factors.  
3. Methotrexate-induced pneumonitis/alveolar haemorrhage – Low-moderate likelihood: on methotrexate, but usually subacute; needs exclusion if infection/PE ruled out.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing elements: objective temperature, blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, lung auscultation findings, comprehensive review of systems, detailed methotrexate dosing schedule, alcohol intake.  
• Conflicts: Patient gave two different names (“Tracy Chapman” vs “Doris”) – conflict noted; clinician proceeded without clarification.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational repetitions but clinically adequate data capture.
